chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
"Rubbing with the thumb and the forefinger at the time of wudu (ablution) is siwak."

key_terms.التَّسْوِيكُ: the act of using siwak or cleansing the teeth
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before worship
key_terms.سِوَاكٌ: siwak, tooth-cleaning regarded here as fulfilled by this action

ai.seo_question: Does rubbing the teeth with the thumb and forefinger during wudu count as siwak?
ai.summary: This hadith states that rubbing with the thumb and forefinger during wudu (ablution) counts as siwak. It indicates a recognized form of oral cleaning connected to ritual purity and the etiquette of preparing for worship.
